commands.doc:
Execute Minecraft commands and gather data from the results. Only available on command computers. Besides `commands.exec`, every command has a helper function, e.g. `commands.say("Hi!")` is equivalent to `commands.exec("say Hi!")`.

```lua
commands.setblock("~", "~1", "~", "minecraft:stone")
```

async.doc:
A table containing asynchronous wrappers for all commands.

As with `commands.execAsync`, this returns the "task id" of the enqueued command.

```lua
commands.async.setblock("~", "~1", "~", "minecraft:stone")
```

exec.doc:
Execute a specific command.

```lua
commands.exec("setblock ~ ~1 ~ minecraft:stone")
```

params.name: command
params.doc: The command to execute.

returns.doc: Whether the command executed successfully.
The output of this command, as a list of lines.
The number of "affected" objects, or `nil` if the command failed. The definition of this varies from command to command.

execAsync.doc:
Asynchronously execute a command.

Unlike `exec`, this will immediately return, instead of waiting for the command to execute. This allows you to run multiple commands at the same time.

```lua
commands.execAsync("setblock ~ ~1 ~ minecraft:stone")
```

params.name: command
params.doc: The command to execute.

returns.doc: The "task id". When this command has been executed, it will queue a `task_complete` event with a matching id.

When a directory is a possible candidate for completion, two entries are included - one with a trailing slash (indicating that entries within this directory exist) and one without it (meaning this entry is an immediate completion candidate). `include_dirs` can be set to `false` to only include those with a trailing slash.

```lua
read(nil, nil, function(str)
    return fs.complete(str, "", true, false)
end)
```

params.doc: The path to complete.

params.name: include_files
params.doc: When `false`, only directories will be included in the returned list. Defaults to `true`.

params.name: include_dirs
params.doc: When `false`, "raw" directories will not be included in the returned list. Defaults to `true`.

returns.doc: A list of possible completion candidates.

params.name: path
params.doc: The path to complete.

params.name: location
params.doc: The location where paths are resolved from.

find.doc:

gps.doc:
Use modems to locate the position of the current turtle or computers.

This works by communicating with other computers (called GPS hosts) that already know their position, finding the distance to those computers (with `modem_message`), and using that to derive its position from theirs (with a process known as [trilateration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilateration).

If this returns `true`, one should also listen for `http_check` which will container further information about whether the URL is allowed or not.

```lua
print(http.checkURL("https://example.tweaked.cc/"))

-- => false Domain not permitted

```

rad.doc: Convert an angle from degrees to radians.

random.doc:
Generate a pseudo-random number. With no arguments, returns a float in [0, 1). With one argument `m`, returns an integer in [1, m]; with two, an integer in [m, n].

```lua
local roll = math.random(1, 6)
```

params.name: m
params.doc: The upper bound (or lower bound, if `n` is given).

params.name: n
params.doc: The upper bound.

returns.doc: The random number.

randomseed.doc: Seed the pseudo-random number generator used by `math.random`.

params.name: x
params.doc: The seed.

multishell.doc:
Multishell allows multiple programs to be run at the same time.

When multiple programs are running, it displays a tab bar at the top of the screen, which allows you to switch between programs. New programs can be launched using the `fg` or `bg` programs, or using the `shell.openTab` and `multishell.launch` functions. Only available on advanced computers when multishell is enabled.

getCount.doc: Get the number of processes within this multishell.

returns.doc: The number of processes.

getCurrent.doc: Get the index of the currently running process.

returns.doc: The currently running process.

getFocus.doc:
Get the currently visible process. This will be the one selected on the tab bar.

Note, this is different to `getCurrent`, which returns the process which is currently executing.

returns.doc: The currently visible process's index.

getTitle.doc:
Get the title of the given tab.

This starts as the name of the program, but may be changed using `multishell.setTitle`.

params.name: n
params.doc: The process index.

returns.doc: The current process title, or `nil` if the process doesn't exist.

launch.doc:
Start a new process, with the given environment, program and arguments.

The returned process index is not constant over the program's run. It can be safely used immediately after launching (for instance, to update the title or switch to that tab). However, after your program has yielded, it may no longer be correct.

```lua
local id = multishell.launch({}, "/rom/programs/fun/hello.lua")
multishell.setTitle(id, "Hello!")
```

params.name: tProgramEnv
params.doc: The environment to load the path under.

params.name: sProgramPath
params.doc: The path to the program to run.
Additional arguments to pass to the program.

returns.doc: The index of the created process.

params.name: n
params.doc: The process index to switch to.

returns.doc: If the process was changed successfully. This will return `false` if there is no process with this id.

setTitle.doc:
Set the title of the given process.

```lua
multishell.setTitle(multishell.getCurrent(), "Hello")
```

params.name: n
params.doc: The process index.

params.name: title
params.doc: The new process title.

next.doc: Get the next key/value pair of a table after `key`. Calling with `key` as `nil` returns the first pair; `next(t) == nil` checks whether a table is empty.

params.name: t
params.doc: The table to traverse.

params.name: key
params.doc: The previous key, or `nil` to start.

returns.doc: The next key, or `nil` when there are no more entries.
The value for that key.

os.doc: The `os` API allows interacting with the current computer: its events and timers, time and date, label and ID, and power state.

cancelAlarm.doc: Cancel an alarm previously started with `os.setAlarm`, stopping it from firing.

params.name: token
params.doc: The ID of the alarm to cancel.

cancelTimer.doc: Cancels a timer previously started with `startTimer`. This will stop the timer from firing.

params.name: token
params.doc: The ID of the timer to cancel.

clock.doc: Returns the number of seconds that the computer has been running.

returns.doc: The computer's uptime.

computerID.doc: Returns the ID of the computer. An alias of `getComputerID`.

returns.doc: The ID of the computer.

computerLabel.doc: Returns the label of the computer, or `nil` if none is set. An alias of `getComputerLabel`.

returns.doc: The label of the computer.

date.doc:
Returns a date string (or table) using a specified format string and optional time to format.

The format string takes the same formats as C's [strftime](http://www.cplusplus.com/reference/ctime/strftime/) function. The format string can also be prefixed with an exclamation mark (`!`) to use UTC time instead of the server's local timezone.

```lua
os.date("%A %d %B %Y") -- See the reference above!
```

params.name: format
params.doc: The format of the string to return. This defaults to `%c`, which expands to a string similar to "Sat Dec 24 16:58:00 2011".

params.name: time
params.doc: The timestamp to convert to a string. This defaults to the current time.

returns.doc: The formatted date string, or a date table if the format was `"*t"` or `"!*t"`.

day.doc: Get the current day, depending on the locale: `"ingame"` (the default) returns the number of days since the world was created, while `"utc"` and `"local"` return the number of days since 1 January 1970 in UTC or the server's timezone.

params.name: locale
params.doc: The locale to get the day for. Defaults to `ingame` if not set.

returns.doc: The day depending on the selected locale.

epoch.doc:
Get the number of milliseconds since an epoch, depending on the locale: `"ingame"` (the default) returns in-game milliseconds since the world was created (72,000 per real second), while `"utc"` and `"local"` return real milliseconds since 1 January 1970.

```lua
local time_table = os.date("*t", os.epoch("local") / 1000)
```

params.name: locale
params.doc: The locale to get the milliseconds for. Defaults to `ingame` if not set.

returns.doc: The milliseconds since the epoch depending on the selected locale.

getComputerID.doc: Returns the ID of the computer.

returns.doc: The ID of the computer.

getComputerLabel.doc: Returns the label of the computer, or `nil` if none is set.

returns.doc: The label of the computer.

loadAPI.doc: Load the given file as an API, placing the resulting table in the global environment under the file's name (without `.lua`).

params.name: path
params.doc: The path of the API to load.

returns.doc: Whether the API was successfully loaded.

loadAPI.deprecated: Pollutes the global table and can mask errors; use `require` instead.

pullEvent.doc:
Wait for an event (optionally only one with the given name) and return its name and parameters. If a `terminate` event is received (Ctrl+T), this raises a `"Terminated"` error.

```lua
local event, key, is_held = os.pullEvent("key")
print(keys.getName(key) .. " was pressed")
```

params.name: filter
params.doc: The event name to wait for. Other events are discarded.

returns.name: event
returns.doc: The name of the event that fired.
The event's parameters.

pullEventRaw.doc:
Wait for an event (optionally only one with the given name) and return its name and parameters. Unlike `os.pullEvent`, this does not error on `terminate` events, allowing programs to handle Ctrl+T themselves.

```lua
local event = os.pullEventRaw("terminate")
print("Caught terminate event!")
```

params.name: filter
params.doc: The event name to wait for. Other events are discarded.

returns.name: event
returns.doc: The name of the event that fired.
The event's parameters.

queueEvent.doc:
Add an event to the event queue, to be picked up later by `os.pullEvent`.

```lua
os.queueEvent("my_event", 1, 2, 3)
print(os.pullEvent("my_event"))
```

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the event to queue.
The parameters of the event. These can be booleans, numbers, strings or tables; functions and metatables are not preserved.

run.doc: Run the program at the given path with the given environment and arguments. Unlike `shell.run`, this does not resolve program names or aliases, and the program has no access to the `shell` API.

params.name: env
params.doc: The environment to run the program with.

params.name: path
params.doc: The exact path of the program to run.
The arguments to pass to the program.

returns.doc: Whether the program ran successfully.

setAlarm.doc: Sets an alarm that will fire at the specified in-game time. When it fires, an `alarm` event will be added to the event queue with the ID returned from this function as the first parameter.

params.name: time
params.doc: The time at which to fire the alarm, in the range [0.0, 24.0).

returns.doc: The ID of the new alarm. This can be used to filter the `alarm` event, or cancel the alarm.

setComputerLabel.doc: Set the label of this computer.

params.name: label
params.doc: The new label. May be `nil` in order to clear it.

sleep.doc: Pause execution for the given number of seconds. An alias of `sleep`.

params.name: time
params.doc: The number of seconds to sleep for, rounded up to the nearest multiple of 0.05.

startTimer.doc: Starts a timer that will run for the specified number of seconds. Once the timer fires, a `timer` event will be added to the queue with the ID returned from this function as the first parameter.

params.name: time
params.doc: The number of seconds until the timer fires.

returns.doc: The ID of the new timer. This can be used to filter the `timer` event, or cancel the timer.

time.doc:
Returns the current time depending on the string passed in. This will always be in the range [0.0, 24.0).

```lua
textutils.formatTime(os.time())
```

params.name: locale
params.doc: The locale (`"ingame"`, `"utc"` or `"local"`), or a table from `os.date("*t")` to convert to a UNIX timestamp. Defaults to `"ingame"`.

returns.doc: The hour of the selected locale, or a UNIX timestamp (in seconds) if a date table was given.

unloadAPI.doc: Unload an API loaded with `os.loadAPI`, removing it from the global environment.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the API to unload.

version.doc: Get the current CraftOS version (for example, `"CraftOS 1.9"`).

returns.doc: The current CraftOS version.

package.doc: The `package` library, created for each program by `cc.require`. It controls how `require` finds and caches modules.

config.doc: A string describing the path configuration (directory separator, template separator, substitution mark, ...), as in standard Lua.

loaded.doc: A table of already-loaded modules, keyed by module name. `require` returns the cached value if present.

loaders.doc: The list of searcher functions `require` uses to find a module: first `package.preload`, then files on `package.path`.

path.doc: A `;`-separated list of path templates used by `require` to find Lua modules. `?` is replaced by the module name (with `.` converted to `/`).

preload.doc: A table of loader functions for specific modules, checked by `require` before searching the file system.

searchpath.doc: Search for `name` in the given `;`-separated path template.

params.name: name
params.doc: The module name to search for.

params.name: path
params.doc: The path templates to search, such as `package.path`.

params.name: sep
params.doc: The separator in `name` to replace. Defaults to `"."`.

params.name: rep
params.doc: The replacement for `sep`. Defaults to `"/"`.

returns.doc: The path of the first file which exists, or `nil` if none was found.
A message listing every path tried.

paintutils.doc: Utilities for drawing more complex graphics, such as pixels, lines and images.

drawBox.doc:
Draws the outline of a box on the current term from the specified start position to the specified end position.

```lua
paintutils.drawBox(2, 3, 30, 7, colors.red)
```

params.name: startX
params.doc: The starting x position of the line.

params.name: startY
params.doc: The starting y position of the line.

params.name: endX
params.doc: The end x position of the line.

params.name: endY
params.doc: The end y position of the line.

params.name: colour
params.doc: The color of this pixel. This will be the current background colour if not specified.

drawFilledBox.doc:
Draws a filled box on the current term from the specified start position to the specified end position.

```lua
paintutils.drawFilledBox(2, 3, 30, 7, colors.red)
```

params.name: startX
params.doc: The starting x position of the line.

params.name: startY

params.doc: The end x position of the line.

params.name: endY
params.doc: The end y position of the line.

params.name: colour
params.doc: The color of this pixel. This will be the current background colour if not specified.

drawImage.doc:
Draw an image loaded by `paintutils.parseImage` or `paintutils.loadImage`.

```lua
local image = paintutils.loadImage("data/example.nfp")
paintutils.drawImage(image, term.getCursorPos())
```

params.name: image

params.name: xPos
params.doc: The x position to start drawing at.

params.name: yPos

Draws a straight line from the start to end position.

```lua
paintutils.drawLine(2, 3, 30, 7, colors.red)
```

params.doc: The end x position of the line.

params.doc: The end y position of the line.

params.name: colour

params.name: yPos
params.doc: The y position to draw at, where 1 is the very top.

params.name: colour
params.doc: The color of this pixel. This will be the current background colour if not specified.

loadImage.doc:
Loads an image from a file.

You can create a file suitable for being loaded using the `paint` program.

```lua
local image = paintutils.loadImage("data/example.nfp")
paintutils.drawImage(image, term.getCursorPos())
```

params.name: path
params.doc: The file to load.

returns.doc: The parsed image data, suitable for use with `paintutils.drawImage`, or `nil` if the file does not exist.

parseImage.doc:
Parses an image from a multi-line string

```lua
local image = paintutils.parseImage([[
 e  e

e    e
 eeee
]])
paintutils.drawImage(image, term.getCursorPos())
```

params.name: image
params.doc: The string containing the raw-image data.

returns.doc: The parsed image data, suitable for use with `paintutils.drawImage`.

pairs.doc:
Return an iterator over every key/value pair of a table (in an unspecified order). Respects the `__pairs` metamethod.

```lua
for k, v in pairs({ a = 1, b = 2 }) do print(k, v) end
```

params.name: t
params.doc: The table to iterate over.

returns.doc: The iterator function (`next`).
The table `t`.
The initial key.

parallel.doc:
A simple way to run several functions at once.

Functions are not actually executed simultaneously, but rather this API will automatically switch between them whenever they yield (e.g. whenever they call `coroutine.yield`, or functions that call that - such as `os.pullEvent` - or functions that call that, etc - basically, anything that causes the function to "pause").

waitForAll.doc:
Runs several functions in parallel, until all of them are finished.

If any of the functions errors, the other functions are not resumed, and the error is propagated upwards.

params.doc: The functions to run in parallel.

waitForAny.doc: Switches between execution of the functions, until any of them finishes. If any of the functions errors, the message is propagated upwards from the `parallel.waitForAny` call.

params.doc: The functions to run in parallel.

pcall.doc:
Call a function in protected mode: any error raised inside it is caught rather than propagated.

```lua
local ok, err = pcall(error, "oops")
print(ok, err) -- false oops
```

params.name: f
params.doc: The function to call.
Arguments to pass to `f`.

returns.doc: `true` if the call succeeded, `false` if it raised an error.
The return values of `f`, or the error message.

peripheral.doc:
Find and control peripherals attached to this computer.

Peripherals are blocks (or turtle and pocket computer upgrades) which can be controlled by a computer. For instance, the `speaker` peripheral allows a computer to play music and the `monitor` peripheral allows you to display text in the world.

call.doc:
Call a method on the peripheral with the given name.

```lua
peripheral.call("top", "open", 1)
```

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the peripheral to invoke the method on.

params.name: method
params.doc: The name of the method
Additional arguments to pass to the method

returns.doc: The return values of the peripheral method.

find.doc:
Find all peripherals of a specific type, and return the wrapped peripherals.

```lua
local monitors = { peripheral.find("monitor") }
for _, monitor in pairs(monitors) do
  monitor.write("Hello")
end
```

The returned tables' methods depend on the peripheral type searched for.

params.name: ty
params.doc: The type of peripheral to look for.

params.name: filter
params.doc: A filter function, which takes the peripheral's name and wrapped table and returns if it should be included in the result.

returns.doc: Zero or more wrapped peripherals matching the given type and filter.

getMethods.doc: Get all available methods for the peripheral with the given name.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the peripheral to find.

returns.doc: A list of methods provided by this peripheral, or `nil` if it is not present.

getName.doc: Get the name of a peripheral wrapped with `peripheral.wrap`.

params.name: peripheral
params.doc: The peripheral to get the name of.

returns.doc: The name of the given peripheral.

getNames.doc:
Provides a list of all peripherals available.

If a device is located directly next to the system, then its name will be listed as the side it is attached to. If a device is attached via a Wired Modem, then it'll be reported according to its name on the wired network.

returns.doc: A list of the names of all attached peripherals.

getType.doc:
Get the types of a named or wrapped peripheral.

```lua
peripheral.getType("top")
```

params.name: peripheral
params.doc: The name of the peripheral to find, or a wrapped peripheral instance.

returns.doc: The peripheral's types, or `nil` if it is not present.

hasType.doc: Check if a peripheral is of a particular type.

params.name: peripheral
params.doc: The name of the peripheral or a wrapped peripheral instance.

params.name: peripheral_type
params.doc: The type to check.

returns.doc: If a peripheral has a particular type, or `nil` if it is not present.

isPresent.doc:
Determines if a peripheral is present with the given name.

```lua
peripheral.isPresent("top")
```

params.name: name
params.doc: The side or network name that you want to check.

returns.doc: If a peripheral is present with the given name.

wrap.doc:
Get a table containing all functions available on a peripheral. These can then be called instead of using `peripheral.call` every time.

```lua
local modem = peripheral.wrap("top")
modem.open(1)
```

The returned table's methods depend on the peripheral type (see `peripheral.getType`), e.g. a `monitor` or `modem`.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the peripheral to wrap.

returns.doc: A table containing the peripheral's methods, or `nil` if no peripheral is present with the given name.

pocket.doc: Control the current pocket computer, adding or removing upgrades. This API is only available on pocket computers, so `if pocket then ... end` can be used to detect one.

equipBack.doc:
Search the player's inventory for another upgrade, replacing the existing one with that item if found.

This inventory search starts from the player's currently selected slot, allowing you to prioritise upgrades.

returns.doc: If an item was equipped.
The reason an item was not equipped.

unequipBack.doc: Remove the pocket computer's current upgrade.

returns.doc: If the upgrade was unequipped.
The reason an upgrade was not unequipped.

print.doc:
Print the given values to the terminal, followed by a new line. Values are converted with `tostring` and separated by tabs; long lines are word-wrapped.

```lua
print("Hello", "world", 123)
```

params.doc: The values to print.

returns.doc: The number of lines written.

printError.doc: Print the given values to the terminal in red (on colour terminals), followed by a new line. Useful for reporting errors.

params.doc: The values to print.

rawequal.doc: Check whether two values are primitively equal, without invoking the `__eq` metamethod.

returns.doc: Whether the values are equal.

params.name: t
params.doc: The table to index.

params.name: k
params.doc: The key.

returns.doc: The raw value.

rawlen.doc: Get the length of a table or string without invoking the `__len` metamethod.

params.name: v
params.doc: The table or string.

returns.doc: The length.

rawset.doc: Set `t[k] = v` without invoking the `__newindex` metamethod.

params.name: t
params.doc: The table to modify.

params.name: k
params.doc: The key.

params.name: v
params.doc: The value.

returns.doc: The table `t`.

read.doc:
Read a line of input from the user, handling cursor movement, history and completion. Blocks until the user presses enter.

```lua
write("Password: ")
local password = read("*")
```

params.name: replaceChar
params.doc: A character to display in place of typed characters, e.g. `"*"` for passwords.

params.name: history

params.name: completeFn

params.name: default
params.doc: Text to pre-fill the input with.

returns.doc: The text the user entered.

rednet.doc: Communicate with other computers by using modems. `rednet` provides a layer of abstraction on top of the main `modem` peripheral, making it slightly easier to use.

broadcast.doc:
Broadcasts a string message over the predefined `CHANNEL_BROADCAST` channel. The message will be received by every device listening to rednet.

```lua
rednet.broadcast("Hello, world!")
```

params.name: message
params.doc: The message to send. This should not contain coroutines or functions, as they will be converted to `nil`.

params.name: protocol
params.doc: The "protocol" to send this message under. When using `rednet.receive` one can filter to only receive messages sent under a particular protocol.

CHANNEL_BROADCAST.doc: The channel used by the Rednet API to `broadcast` messages.

CHANNEL_REPEAT.doc: The channel used by the Rednet API to repeat messages.

close.doc: Close a modem with the given `peripheral` name, meaning it can no longer send and receive rednet messages.

params.name: modem
params.doc: The side the modem exists on. If not given, all open modems will be closed.

host.doc: Register the system as "hosting" the desired protocol under the specified name. If a rednet lookup is performed for that protocol (and maybe name) on the same network, the registered system will automatically respond via a background process, hence providing the system performing the lookup with its ID number.

params.name: protocol
params.doc: The protocol this computer provides.

params.name: hostname
params.doc: The name this computer exposes for the given protocol.

isOpen.doc: Determine if rednet is currently open.

params.name: modem
params.doc: Which modem to check. If not given, all connected modems will be checked.

returns.doc: If the given modem is open.

lookup.doc:
Search the local rednet network for systems hosting the desired protocol and returns any computer IDs that respond as "registered" against it.

If a hostname is specified, only one ID will be returned (assuming an exact match is found).

```lua
local computers = {rednet.lookup("chat")}
print(#computers .. " computers available to chat")
for _, computer in pairs(computers) do
  print("Computer #" .. computer)
end
```

params.name: protocol
params.doc: The protocol to search for.

params.name: hostname
params.doc: The hostname to search for.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: The number of seconds to wait for a lookup response. Defaults to `2`.

returns.doc: Without a hostname: the IDs of every computer hosting the protocol (as multiple return values). With a hostname: the ID of the matching computer, or `nil` if none was found.

MAX_ID_CHANNELS.doc: The number of channels rednet reserves for computer IDs. Computers with IDs greater or equal to this limit wrap around to 0.

open.doc:
Opens a modem with the given `peripheral` name, allowing it to send and receive messages over rednet.

This will open the modem on two channels: one which has the same ID as the computer, and another on the broadcast channel.

```lua
rednet.open("back")
```

params.name: modem
params.doc: The name of the modem to open.

receive.doc:
Wait for a rednet message to be received, or until `timeout` seconds have elapsed.

```lua
local id, message = rednet.receive()
print(("Computer %d sent message %s"):format(id, message))
```

params.name: protocol_filter
params.doc: The protocol the received message must be sent with. If specified, any messages not sent under this protocol will be discarded.

params.name: timeout
params.doc: The number of seconds to wait if no message is received.

returns.doc: `number`: The computer which sent this message. Or `nil`: If the timeout elapsed and no message was received.
The received message
The protocol this message was sent under.

run.doc:
Listen for modem messages and converts them into rednet messages, which may then be received.

This is automatically started in the background on computer startup, and should not be called manually.

send.doc:
Allows a computer or turtle with an attached modem to send a message intended for a computer with a specific ID. At least one such modem must first be opened before sending is possible.

```lua
rednet.send(2, "Hello from rednet!")
```

params.name: recipient
params.doc: The ID of the receiving computer.

params.name: message
params.doc: The message to send. Like with `modem.transmit`, this can contain any primitive type (numbers, booleans and strings) as well as tables. Other types (like functions), as well as metatables, will not be transmitted.

params.name: protocol
params.doc: The "protocol" to send this message under. When using `rednet.receive` one can filter to only receive messages sent under a particular protocol.

returns.doc: If this message was successfully sent (i.e. if rednet is currently open). Note, this does not guarantee the message was actually _received_.

unhost.doc: Stop hosting a specific protocol, meaning it will no longer respond to `rednet.lookup` requests.

params.name: protocol
params.doc: The protocol to unregister your self from.

redstone.doc:
Get and set redstone signals adjacent to this computer: simple on/off signals, analogue strengths (0-15) and bundled cables. A `redstone` event fires whenever an input changes. Also available as `rs`.

```lua
while true do
  redstone.setOutput("top", not redstone.getOutput("top"))
  sleep(0.5)
end
```

params.name: side
params.doc: The side to get.

returns.doc: The input signal strength, between 0 and 15.

getAnalogOutput.doc: Get the redstone output signal strength for a specific side.

params.name: side
params.doc: The side to get.

returns.doc: The output signal strength, between 0 and 15.

getAnalogueInput.doc: Get the redstone input signal strength for a specific side. An alias of `getAnalogInput`.

params.name: side
params.doc: The side to get.

returns.doc: The input signal strength, between 0 and 15.

getAnalogueOutput.doc: Get the redstone output signal strength for a specific side. An alias of `getAnalogOutput`.

params.name: side
params.doc: The side to get.

returns.doc: The output signal strength, between 0 and 15.

getBundledInput.doc: Get the bundled cable input for a specific side.

params.name: side
params.doc: The side to get.

returns.doc: The bundle cable's input.

getBundledOutput.doc: Get the bundled cable output for a specific side.

params.name: side
params.doc: The side to get.

returns.doc: The bundle cable's output.

getInput.doc: Get the current redstone input of a specific side.

settings.doc:
Read and write configuration options for CraftOS and your programs.

When a computer starts, it reads the current value of settings from the `/.settings` file. These values then may be read or modified.

params.type: { description? = string, default? = any, type? = string }
params.doc:
Options for this setting. This table accepts the following fields:
- `description`: A description which may be printed when running the `set` program.
- `default`: A default value, which is returned by `settings.get` if the setting has not been changed.
- `type`: Require values to be of this type. Setting the value to another type will error. Must be one of: `"number"`, `"string"`, `"boolean"`, or `"table"`.

params.name: name

shell.doc:
The shell API provides access to CraftOS's command line interface.

It allows you to start programs, add completion for a program, and much more.

aliases.doc:
Get the current aliases for this shell.

Aliases are used to allow multiple commands to refer to a single program. For instance, the `list` program is aliased to `dir` or `ls`. Running `ls`, `dir` or `list` in the shell will all run the `list` program.

returns.doc: A table, where the keys are the names of aliases, and the values are the path to the program.

params.name: command
params.doc: The alias name to remove.

complete.doc:
Complete a shell command line.

This accepts an incomplete command, and completes the program name or arguments. For instance, `l` will be completed to `ls`, and `ls ro` will be completed to `ls rom/`.

params.name: sLine
params.doc: The input to complete.

returns.doc: The list of possible completions.

completeProgram.doc: Complete the name of a program.

params.name: program
params.doc: The name of a program to complete.

returns.doc: A list of possible completions.

dir.doc: Return the current working directory. This is what is displayed before the `> ` of the shell prompt, and is used by `shell.resolve` to handle relative paths.

returns.doc: The current working directory.

execute.doc:
Run a program with the supplied arguments.

Unlike `shell.run`, each argument is passed to the program verbatim. While `shell.run("echo", "b c")` runs `echo` with `b` and `c`, `shell.execute("echo", "b c")` runs `echo` with a single argument `b c`.

```lua
shell.execute("paint", "my-image")
```

params.name: command
params.doc: The program to execute.
Arguments to this program.

returns.doc: Whether the program exited successfully.

exit.doc:
Exit the current shell.

This does _not_ terminate your program, it simply makes the shell terminate after your program has finished. If this is the toplevel shell, then the computer will be shutdown.

getCompletionInfo.doc:
Get a table containing all completion functions.

This should only be needed when building custom shells. Use `setCompletionFunction` to add a completion function.

returns.doc: A table mapping the absolute path of programs, to their completion functions.

getRunningProgram.doc: Returns the path to the currently running program.

returns.doc: The absolute path to the running program.

openTab.doc:
Open a new `multishell` tab running a command.

This behaves similarly to `shell.run`, but instead returns the process index.

This function is only available if the `multishell` API is.

```lua
local id = shell.openTab("lua")
shell.switchTab(id)
```

params.doc: The command line to run.

returns.doc: The ID of the new tab that was opened.

path.doc:
Get the path where programs are located.

The path is composed of a list of directory names in a string, each separated by a colon (`:`). On normal turtles will look in the current directory (`.`), `/rom/programs` and `/rom/programs/turtle` folder, making the path `.:/rom/programs:/rom/programs/turtle`.

returns.doc: The current shell's path.

programs.doc:
Return a list of all programs on the path.

```lua
textutils.tabulate(shell.programs())
```

params.name: include_hidden
params.doc: Include hidden files. Namely, any which start with `.`.

returns.doc: A list of available programs.

resolve.doc:
Resolve a relative path to an absolute path.

The `fs` and `io` APIs work using absolute paths, and so we must convert any paths relative to the current directory to absolute ones. This does nothing when the path starts with `/`.

```lua
shell.setDir("rom")
print(shell.resolve("startup.lua"))
-- => rom/startup.lua
```

params.name: path
params.doc: The path to resolve.

returns.doc: The absolute path.

resolveProgram.doc:
Resolve a program, using the program path and list of aliases.

```lua
shell.resolveProgram("hello")
-- => rom/programs/fun/hello.lua
```

params.name: command
params.doc: The name of the program

returns.doc: The absolute path to the program, or `nil` if it could not be found.

run.doc:
Run a program with the supplied arguments.

All arguments are concatenated together and then parsed as a command line. As a result, `shell.run("program a b")` is the same as `shell.run("program", "a", "b")`.

```lua
shell.run("paint", "my-image")
```

params.doc: The program to run and its arguments.

returns.doc: Whether the program exited successfully.

setAlias.doc:
Add an alias for a program.

```lua
shell.setAlias("vim", "edit")
```

params.name: command
params.doc: The name of the alias to add.

params.name: program
params.doc: The name or path to the program.

setCompletionFunction.doc: Set the completion function for a program. When the program is entered on the command line, this function is called to provide auto-complete information. It receives the current shell, the index of the argument being completed, the current (possibly empty) argument and a list of the previous arguments, and should return a list of completion suffixes. See `cc.shell.completion` for helpers.

params.name: program
params.doc: The path to the program. This should be an absolute path _without_ the leading `/`.

cc.audio.dfpwm.doc:
Convert between streams of DFPWM audio data and a list of amplitudes.

DFPWM (Dynamic Filter Pulse Width Modulation) is an audio codec designed by GreaseMonkey. It's a relatively compact format compared to raw PCM data, only using 1 bit per sample, but is simple enough to encode and decode in real time.

decode.doc:
A convenience function for decoding a complete file of audio at once.

This should only be used for short files. For larger files, one should read the file in chunks and process it using `make_decoder`.

params.name: input
params.doc: The DFPWM data to convert.

returns.doc: The produced amplitude data.

encode.doc:
A convenience function for encoding a complete file of audio at once.

This should only be used for complete pieces of audio. If you are writing multiple chunks to the same place, you should use an encoder returned by `make_encoder` instead.

params.name: input
params.doc: The table of amplitude data.

returns.doc: The encoded DFPWM data.

make_decoder.doc:
Create a new decoder for converting DFPWM into PCM audio data. The returned decoder is itself a function, which accepts a string and returns a table of amplitudes between -128 and 127.

```lua
local speaker = peripheral.find("speaker")
local decoder = require("cc.audio.dfpwm").make_decoder()
for chunk in io.lines("data/example.dfpwm", 16 * 1024) do
  local buffer = decoder(chunk)
  while not speaker.playAudio(buffer) do os.pullEvent("speaker_audio_empty") end
end
```

returns.doc: The decoder function.

make_encoder.doc:
Create a new encoder for converting PCM audio data into DFPWM.

The returned encoder is itself a function. This function accepts a table of amplitude data between -128 and 127 and returns the encoded DFPWM data.

returns.doc: The encoder function

Documents effectively represent a sequence of strings in alternative layouts, which we will try to print in the most compact form necessary. Documents can be concatenated with `..` and converted to a string with `tostring`.

Returns an iterator that, each time it is called, returns a new line from the file.

This can be used in a for loop to iterate over all lines of a file

Once the end of the file has been reached, `nil` will be returned. The file is *not* automatically closed.

```lua
local file = io.open("/rom/help/intro.txt")
for line in file:lines() do
  print(line)
end
file:close()
```

read.doc:
Reads data from the file, using the specified formats. For each format provided, the function returns either the data read, or `nil` if no data could be read.

The following formats are available:
- `l`: Returns the next line (without a newline on the end).
- `L`: Returns the next line (with a newline on the end).
- `a`: Returns the entire rest of the file.
- ~~`n`: Returns a number~~ (not implemented in CC).

params.doc: The formats to use.

returns.doc: The data read from the file.

seek.doc:
Seeks the file cursor to the specified position, and returns the new position.

`whence` controls where the seek operation starts, and is a string that may be one of these three values:
- `set`: base position is 0 (beginning of the file)
- `cur`: base is current position
- `end`: base is end of file

params.name: whence
params.doc: The place to set the cursor from.

params.name: offset
params.doc: The offset from the start to move to.

returns.doc: The new location of the file cursor.

Each tank either contains some amount of fluid or is empty. Tanks with fluids inside will return some basic information about the fluid, including its name and amount.

getItemDetail.doc: Get detailed information about an item.

params.doc: The slot to get information about.

returns.doc: Information about the item in this slot, or `nil` if it is empty.

getItemLimit.doc:
Get the maximum number of items which can be stored in this slot.

Typically this will be limited to 64 items. However, some inventories (such as barrels or caches) can store hundreds or thousands of items in one slot.

```lua
local chest = peripheral.find("minecraft:chest")
local total = 0
for i = 1, chest.size() do
  total = total + chest.getItemLimit(i)
end
print(total)
```

params.name: slot
params.doc: The slot

returns.doc: The maximum number of items in this slot.

list.doc:
List all items in this inventory. This returns a table, with an entry for each slot.

Each item in the inventory is represented by a table containing some basic information. More information can be fetched with `getItemDetail`. The table contains the item `name`, the `count` and an a (potentially nil) hash of the item's `nbt.` This NBT data doesn't contain anything useful, but allows you to distinguish identical items.

```lua
local chest = peripheral.find("minecraft:chest")
for slot, item in pairs(chest.list()) do
  print(("%d x %s in slot %d"):format(item.count, item.name, slot))
end
```

returns.doc: Basic information about all items in this inventory.

pullItems.doc:
Pull items from a connected inventory into this one.

This allows you to transfer items between inventories *on the same wired network*. Both this and the source inventory must attached to wired modems which are connected via a cable.

```lua
local chest_a = peripheral.wrap("minecraft:chest_0")
local chest_b = peripheral.wrap("minecraft:chest_1")

chest_a.pullItems(peripheral.getName(chest_b), 1)
```

params.doc: The name of the peripheral/inventory to pull from. This is the string given to `peripheral.wrap`, and displayed by the wired modem.

params.name: fromSlot

pushItems.doc:
Push items from one inventory to another connected one.

This allows you to push an item in an inventory to another inventory *on the same wired network*. Both inventories must attached to wired modems which are connected via a cable.

```lua
local chest_a = peripheral.wrap("minecraft:chest_0")
local chest_b = peripheral.wrap("minecraft:chest_1")

chest_a.pushItems(peripheral.getName(chest_b), 1)
```

modem.doc:
Modems allow you to send messages between computers over long distances. Wired modems additionally provide methods for accessing peripherals on their network (`getNamesRemote`, `callRemote`, ...).

```lua
local modem = peripheral.find("modem") or error("No modem attached", 0)
modem.open(15)
modem.transmit(15, 43, "Hello, world!")
```

*Wired modems only.*

params.name: remoteName

*Wired modems only.*

List all remote peripherals on the wired network.

If this computer is attached to the network, it _will not_ be included in this list.

Determine if this is a wired or wireless modem.

Some methods (namely those dealing with wired networks and remote peripherals) are only available on wired modems.

open.doc: Open a channel on a modem. A channel must be open in order to receive messages. Modems can have up to 128 channels open at one time.

transmit.doc:
Sends a modem message on a certain channel. Modems listening on the channel will queue a `modem_message` event on adjacent computers.

```lua
local modem = peripheral.find("modem") or error("No modem attached", 0)
modem.transmit(15, 43, "Hello, world!")
```

params.name: payload
params.doc: The object to send. This can be any primitive type (boolean, number, string) as well as tables. Other types (like functions), as well as metatables, will not be transmitted.

Monitors are a block which act as a terminal, displaying information on one side. This allows them to be read and interacted with in-world without opening a GUI.

```lua

monitor.write("Hello, world!")
```

redstone_relay.doc:
The redstone relay is a peripheral that allows reading and outputting redstone signals. While this is not very useful on its own (as computers have the same functionality built-in), this can be used with wired modems to interact with multiple redstone signals from the same computer.

```lua
local relay = peripheral.find("redstone_relay")
while true do
  relay.setOutput("top", not relay.getOutput("top"))
  sleep(0.5)
end
```

speaker.doc:
The speaker peripheral allows your computer to play notes and other sounds.

The speaker can play three kinds of sound, in increasing orders of complexity:
- `playNote` allows you to play noteblock note.
- `playSound` plays any Minecraft sound, such as block sounds or mob noises.
- `playAudio` can play arbitrary audio.

playAudio.doc:
Attempt to stream some audio data to the speaker.

This accepts a list of audio samples as amplitudes between -128 and 127. These are stored in an internal buffer and played back at 48kHz. If this buffer is full, this function will return false. Programs should wait for a `speaker_audio_empty` event before trying to play audio again.

params.name: audio
params.doc: A list of amplitudes.

params.name: volume
params.doc: The volume to play this audio at. If not given, defaults to the previous volume given to `playAudio`.

returns.doc: If there was room to accept this audio data.

playNote.doc:
Plays a note block note through the speaker.

This takes the name of a note to play, as well as optionally the volume and pitch to play the note at.

The pitch argument uses semitones as the unit. This directly maps to the number of clicks on a note block. For reference, 0, 12, and 24 map to F#, and 6 and 18 map to C.

params.name: instrument
params.doc: The instrument to use to play this note.

params.name: volume
params.doc: The volume to play the note at, from 0.0 to 3.0. Defaults to 1.0.

params.name: pitch
params.doc: The pitch to play the note at in semitones, from 0 to 24. Defaults to 12.

returns.doc: Whether the note could be played as the limit was reached.

playSound.doc:
Plays a Minecraft sound through the speaker.

This takes the name of a [vanilla Minecraft](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Sounds.json) or modded sound, such as `"minecraft:block.note_block.harp"`, as well as an optional volume and pitch.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the sound to play.

params.name: volume
params.doc: The volume to play the sound at, from 0.0 to 3.0. Defaults to 1.0.

params.name: pitch
params.doc: The speed to play the sound at, from 0.5 to 2.0. Defaults to 1.0.

returns.doc: Whether the sound could be played.

stop.doc:
Stop all audio being played by this speaker.

This clears any audio that `playAudio` had queued and stops the latest sound played by `playSound`.

params.doc: The mouse button that is being held.

params.name: x
params.doc: The X coordinate of the mouse, in characters.

params.name: y
params.doc: The Y coordinate of the mouse, in characters.

mouse_scroll.doc: Fired when a mouse wheel is scrolled in the terminal (advanced computers only).

params.name: direction
params.doc: The direction of the scroll: -1 = up, 1 = down.

params.name: x
params.doc: The X coordinate of the mouse, in characters.

params.name: y
params.doc: The Y coordinate of the mouse, in characters.

mouse_up.doc: Fired when a mouse button is released or a held mouse leaves the computer's terminal (advanced computers only).

params.name: button
params.doc: The mouse button that was released.

params.name: x
params.doc: The X coordinate of the mouse, in characters.

params.name: y
params.doc: The Y coordinate of the mouse, in characters.

paste.doc: Fired when text is pasted into the computer through Ctrl+V (or ⌘V on macOS).

params.name: text
params.doc: The text that was pasted.

peripheral.doc: Fired when a peripheral is attached on a side or to a modem.

params.name: side
params.doc: The side (or network name) the peripheral was attached to.

peripheral_detach.doc: Fired when a peripheral is detached from a side or from a modem.

params.name: side
params.doc: The side (or network name) the peripheral was detached from.

rednet_message.doc: Fired when a message is sent over Rednet. Usually you would use `rednet.receive` rather than pulling this event directly.

params.name: sender
params.doc: The ID of the sending computer.

params.name: message
params.doc: The message sent.

params.name: protocol
params.doc: The protocol of the message, if provided.

redstone.doc: Fired whenever any redstone inputs on the computer (or an attached redstone relay) change.

setting_changed.doc: Fired when a setting is changed with `settings.set`, `settings.unset`, `settings.clear` or `settings.load`.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the setting that changed.

params.name: new_value
params.doc: The new value of the setting (`nil` if it was unset).

params.name: old_value
params.doc: The previous value of the setting.

speaker_audio_empty.doc: Fired when the speaker's audio buffer has room for more audio after a call to `speaker.playAudio`.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the speaker which is available to play more audio.

task_complete.doc: Fired when an asynchronous task completes. This is usually handled inside the function that started the task, but some functions (such as `commands.execAsync`) return the task ID directly.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the task that completed.

params.name: success
params.doc: Whether the command succeeded.
If the task failed, an error message; otherwise, the values returned by the task.

term_resize.doc: Fired when the main terminal is resized, for instance when a monitor the terminal is redirected to changes size, or a new monitor is attached.

terminate.doc: Fired when Ctrl+T is held down. It is used to stop programs: `os.pullEvent` raises a `"Terminated"` error when it receives this event; use `os.pullEventRaw` to handle it yourself.

timer.doc:
Fired when a timer started with `os.startTimer` completes.

```lua
local id = os.startTimer(2)
local _, timer_id
repeat _, timer_id = os.pullEvent("timer") until timer_id == id
```

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the timer that finished.

turtle_inventory.doc: Fired when a turtle's inventory is changed.

websocket_closed.doc: Fired when an open websocket closes.

params.name: url
params.doc: The URL of the websocket that was closed.

params.name: reason
params.doc: The server-provided reason the websocket was closed, if any.

params.name: code
params.doc: The connection close code, if provided.

websocket_failure.doc: Fired when a websocket connection request (from `http.websocketAsync`) fails.

params.name: url
params.doc: The URL of the site requested.

params.name: err
params.doc: An error describing the failure.

websocket_message.doc: Fired when a message is received on an open websocket.

params.name: url
params.doc: The URL of the websocket.

params.name: message
params.doc: The contents of the message.

params.name: binary
params.doc: Whether this is a binary message.

websocket_success.doc: Fired when a websocket connection request (from `http.websocketAsync`) returns successfully.

params.name: url
params.doc: The URL of the site.

params.name: handle
params.doc: The handle for the websocket.
